# Blocks world (blocks-world): Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `blocks-world.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `blocks-world-rules.soar` (11 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . blocks-world.soar --seed 1 --cap 200000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . blocks-world.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py blocks-world init-blocksworld.world

`gen.py` regenerates the rules (`tools/rosie_tasks.py`, function `blocks_world`); `python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with
another example state as the initial world, for the state checks.

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states | init-blocksworld: goal false; final-blocksworld: goal true |
| Seeds 1-3, library defaults | solved, 4 moves each (the shortest), 3,288 / 1,373 / 2,870 decisions |
| Independent replay | every move legal, goal holds |
| Settings probe (P6) | operator depth: 12 moves over 3 seeds, 7,528 decisions. Tie-impasse had not finished three seeds after 38 minutes (cap 200,000 decisions per seed) and was stopped; on sorting, the same setting solved 1 of 3 seeds within the cap. Library defaults kept |

## Assumption ledger (places where the English is open)

| ID | Reading |
|---|---|
| A-H1 | "clear" is defined for a location ("If a location is not below an object") but used for "a clear block". Read as: any object that is not below an object is clear. |
| A-H4 | "move X onto Y": X's on relation and the matching below relation now name Y; the object X left becomes clear. |
| A-B1 | "a red block is on a green block and the red block is below a orange block": the same red block in both parts; any blocks of those colors (the world has one of each). |
| A-B2 | The action has no name in the dialog; it is called `move`. |

Convention notes: `clear` is a maintained one-argument relation; the goal is one positive elaboration on the task object.
